andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces a 46% southwest-monsoon rainfall deficit, raising kharif and water-supply concerns
facts: For June 1–September 5, Andhra Pradesh recorded 204.8 mm rainfall against a normal 378.6 mm, a 46% deficit, according to IMD figures reported on September 8.
The report said 23 of the State’s 26 districts had deficient rainfall.
Below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures were forecast over much of the State during September.
The shortfall heightened concerns about kharif cultivation, reservoir storage and drinking-water availability.
andhraPradesh.summary: A September 8 report, citing IMD data, highlighted severe monsoon shortfalls across Andhra Pradesh and the resulting risks to agriculture and water resources. It also reported a forecast of below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures for much of the State during September.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Southwest monsoon; El Niño and Indian climate; rain-fed agriculture; drought preparedness and water-resource management.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the reported 46% rainfall deficit for June 1–September 5, 2026, and the reported deficient rainfall in 23 of 26 districts.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how rainfall variability affects Andhra Pradesh’s kharif economy, irrigation demand and drinking-water security, and discuss district-level contingency planning.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Directly concerns Andhra Pradesh’s rainfall, districts, agriculture and water resources.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh completes land acquisition for 228 feeder-level solar plants under PM-KUSUM
facts: Andhra Pradesh is implementing 228 feeder-level solar plants with a combined capacity of 1,162.8 MW under PM-KUSUM Component C.

The Energy Department’s review reported that land acquisition was complete for all 228 plants; civil works, equipment procurement, financial closure and statutory documentation remained project-level implementation tasks.
The State set an immediate target to commission 109.7 MW during September and October 2026.
The review reported 49 plants totalling 191.5 MW under APCPDCL, 33 plants totalling 220.3 MW under APEPDCL, and 146 plants totalling 751 MW under APSPDCL and KRECS.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Andhra Pradesh’s 1,162.8-MW feeder-solarisation programme under PM-KUSUM was already being tracked. Today: a September 7 progress review reported land acquisition completed for all 228 plants and set a 109.7-MW commissioning target for September–October; construction and other implementation work remained underway.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: PM-KUSUM; decentralised renewable energy; agricultural feeder solarisation; energy security and sustainable development.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: PM-KUSUM Component C supports feeder-level solarisation; distinguish completed land acquisition from solar plants that are commissioned or operational.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how feeder-level solarisation can improve agricultural power supply and reduce conventional-energy dependence, while identifying execution, financing and grid-integration challenges.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The programme covers 228 solar plants across Andhra Pradesh and is being implemented by the State DISCOMs and KRECS.

andhraPradesh.headline: IIT Kanpur reports Phase 1 findings of AI-based Family Score developed with Andhra Pradesh
facts: IIT Kanpur reported Phase 1 findings for Family Score, an AI-powered system intended to assess household socio-economic conditions using existing government data.
The collaboration between IIT Kanpur and the Government of Andhra Pradesh tested whether the system could provide an alternative to conventional household surveys for welfare identification.
The reported next phase would extend the system to households across Andhra Pradesh and integrate it into the State Data Centre.
The project’s stated use is to help identify households that may require welfare support; it does not itself constitute a newly announced cash-benefit scheme.
andhraPradesh.summary: IIT Kanpur reported the Phase 1 findings of its Family Score collaboration with Andhra Pradesh on September 8. The reported next phase would scale the system statewide and integrate it into the AP State Data Centre, making data governance and safeguards relevant to its welfare use.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Artificial intelligence in public administration; targeted welfare delivery; digital governance; data protection and social justice.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Family Score is an AI/ML-based household vulnerability assessment initiative developed with Andhra Pradesh; its reported Phase 1 tested welfare identification using existing government data.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss the potential of data-driven welfare targeting alongside risks of privacy infringement, biased data, exclusion errors and weak accountability.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The system was tested through a collaboration between IIT Kanpur and the Government of Andhra Pradesh, with a reported plan for statewide integration.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh High Court orders conditional release of rice seized from Nellore mill
facts: In M/s Annapurna Raw and Boiled Rice Mill v. State of Andhra Pradesh, Writ Petition No. 25631 of 2026, the Andhra Pradesh High Court considered seizure of rice and proceedings under Section 6A of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
The case involved 900 bags of Swarna raw rice, each weighing 50 kg, seized by Civil Supplies authorities.
Justice K. Sreenivasa Reddy directed release of the stock subject to security equivalent to its value and collection of samples in the petitioner’s presence.
The order concerned interim release pending disposal of the statutory proceedings; it did not decide the underlying proceedings on their merits.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Andhra Pradesh High Court issued a conditional-release direction in a writ petition concerning seized rice stock. The direction protected the interests of both sides while the related proceedings under Section 6A of the Essential Commodities Act continued.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Article 226 judicial review; Essential Commodities Act, 1955; administrative action and procedural safeguards.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The order applied Article 226 jurisdiction in a matter involving Section 6A of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, and made release conditional on security and sampling.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Consider the balance between enforcement of essential-commodities controls and procedural fairness when authorities seize perishable or marketable goods.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The judgment concerns Andhra Pradesh Civil Supplies authorities and a rice mill case involving the Nellore Collector (Civil Supplies).

> Exam angle: Test the **Article 226** order’s conditions and distinguish interim release from a final decision on the statutory proceedings.

national.headline: Dedicated Freight Corridor network becomes fully operational after commissioning of final Western DFC sections
facts: The Prime Minister dedicated three Western Dedicated Freight Corridor sections, spanning 326 route-km, to the nation.
The sections—New Sanand (North)–New Makarpura, New Umbergaon–New Saphale and New Saphale–New JNPT—were developed at a cost exceeding ₹20,700 crore.
Commissioning these sections made the Dedicated Freight Corridor network fully operational across its entire length.
The completed DFC network is approximately 2,800 km and is intended to improve freight movement and port connectivity.
national.summary: On 8 September, the final sections of the Western DFC were dedicated to the nation, completing the operational DFC network. The development strengthens freight logistics and connectivity between industrial centres and ports. No direct AP-specific link established.
national.staticLink: Dedicated freight corridors, multimodal logistics and transport infrastructure
national.prelimsTakeaway: Know the DFC’s purpose in separating freight and passenger traffic; the final commissioned sections connect with JNPT.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how dedicated freight corridors can reduce logistics costs, improve port connectivity and support regional economic development.

national.headline: India’s reported kharif sown area reaches 1,086.31 lakh hectares
facts: The Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Ministry reported 1,086.31 lakh hectares under kharif crops as of 4 September 2026.
The corresponding reported area in 2025 was 1,104.00 lakh hectares, a year-on-year decrease of 17.69 lakh hectares.
Pulses coverage was 117.13 lakh hectares, compared with 115.30 lakh hectares in the corresponding period of 2025.
Rice coverage was 421.82 lakh hectares, compared with 438.19 lakh hectares a year earlier.
national.summary: The Ministry released its weekly kharif area report on 8 September, with coverage measured as of 4 September. Total reported sown area was below the comparable 2025 figure, while pulses recorded a modest increase. No direct AP-specific link established.
national.staticLink: Indian cropping seasons, agricultural geography and crop-area statistics
national.prelimsTakeaway: The figures are progressive area-sown estimates, not final production or yield data; the reference date is 4 September 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how crop-area trends inform food-security planning, agricultural policy and responses to monsoon variability.

national.headline: Seventh Global Fintech Fest opens in Mumbai with a focus on AI, tokenisation and quantum technologies
facts: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the seventh Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on 8 September 2026.
The fest is scheduled for 8–11 September 2026 and brings together policymakers, regulators, financial institutions, fintech firms, technology companies and other stakeholders.
The 2026 theme is “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum: Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.”
The Prime Minister called for stronger cybersecurity, ethical data-protection standards, a regulator–industry innovation ecosystem and a fintech consumer-protection index.
national.summary: The fest opened in Mumbai on 8 September and is scheduled to run through 11 September. The discussions place emerging technologies alongside inclusion, consumer protection and trust in digital finance. No direct AP-specific link established.

national.prelimsTakeaway: GFF 2026 is the seventh edition; its theme combines Agentic AI, tokenisation and quantum technologies with trusted and inclusive finance.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how innovation in fintech can expand financial inclusion while requiring effective consumer protection, data governance and cybersecurity.

national.headline: DFPD and FCI sign performance-focused MoU for foodgrain management in FY 2026–27
facts: The Department of Food and Public Distribution and the Food Corporation of India signed an MoU for FY 2026–27 in New Delhi.
The framework sets targets for storage-loss reduction, storage-capacity use, logistics, supply chains and quality control.
It promotes digitisation and modern information-technology systems for operational monitoring and transparency.
Some depot-performance targets are linked to the Depot Darpan Portal, which assesses depot infrastructure and operational efficiency.
national.summary: The 8 September MoU establishes performance benchmarks for FCI’s foodgrain-management functions for FY 2026–27. The agreement includes depot-level monitoring through the Depot Darpan Portal; it is a performance framework, not a report that its targets have already been achieved. No direct AP-specific link established.

national.prelimsTakeaway: The MoU is between DFPD and FCI; Depot Darpan is used for depot infrastructure and operational assessment.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how digitisation, measurable performance targets and logistics improvements can strengthen foodgrain management and reduce public-system inefficiencies.

national.headline: India and Japan announce bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian-2026 at Jodhpur
facts: The Indian Air Force and Japan Air Self-Defence Force announced Veer Guardian-2026, scheduled for 9–22 September 2026.
The exercise is to be held at Air Force Station Jodhpur, Rajasthan.
The IAF is to field indigenous LCA Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale aircraft; the JASDF is to field F-2A fighters.
Planned activities include operational missions, mission-planning conferences and professional exchanges on engineering and aerospace safety.
national.summary: The Ministry of Defence announced the bilateral exercise on 8 September, with activity scheduled to begin the following day. national.headline: India and Morocco hold inaugural Joint Defence Committee meeting in New Delhi
facts: India and Morocco held their inaugural Joint Defence Committee meeting in New Delhi on 8 September 2026.
The meeting was co-chaired by Ministry of Defence Joint Secretary Amitabh Prasad and Moroccan Royal Armed Forces Brigadier General Abdellah Athmani.
Discussions covered training, education, peacekeeping, military exercises, medical cooperation, cyber defence and defence industries.
The sides agreed to explore co-production, joint ventures, technology collaboration, maintenance and sustainment; bilateral cooperation was approaching its 70th anniversary in 2027.
national.summary: The inaugural committee meeting on 8 September gave institutional form to India–Morocco defence engagement. The sides discussed cooperation areas and agreed to explore further industrial and technical collaboration; no completed joint project was announced. No direct AP-specific link established.
national.staticLink: India’s relations with Africa and institutional defence cooperation
national.prelimsTakeaway: The meeting is an India–Morocco bilateral defence mechanism; its agenda included cyber defence and defence-industrial cooperation.
national.mainsAngle: Analyse how institutional dialogue and defence-industry partnerships can diversify India’s international defence relationships.

national.headline: IAF announces Dronathon-2026 to assess domestic unmanned and counter-drone systems
facts: The Indian Air Force announced Dronathon-2026, scheduled for 14–16 September at the Pokhran range in Jaisalmer.
The event is intended to let domestic manufacturers demonstrate unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and counter-UAS capabilities.
The programme is to include static displays and live demonstrations, with focus areas including surveillance, reconnaissance, autonomy, swarms and electronic warfare.
The stated aim is to assess operational solutions and strengthen India’s indigenous defence ecosystem in line with Atmanirbhar Bharat.

national.headline: Ninth Rashtriya Poshan Maah announced with Anganwadi-centred theme
facts: The Ministry of Women and Child Development announced that the ninth Rashtriya Poshan Maah would be launched on 9 September 2026 in Varanasi.
The 2026 theme is “Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari,” focusing on shared community ownership of Anganwadi centres.
The campaign highlights dietary diversity and protein intake, complementary feeding, maternal nutrition, child development and community accountability.
POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched in March 2018; its interventions were consolidated with Anganwadi Services and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls under Mission Poshan 2.0.
national.summary: A PIB backgrounder published on 8 September outlined the ninth Poshan Maah and its scheduled launch the next day. The campaign is designed to reinforce nutrition and early-childhood-development priorities through Anganwadi-centred community action; it had not yet been launched on the date of this announcement. national.headline: MoSPI launches portal to track harmonisation of administrative data across government
facts: MoSPI held a workshop on harmonising administrative data for data-driven governance on 8 September 2026 in New Delhi.
The Quarterly Progress Report portal on Data Harmonisation was launched for Central Ministries, Departments and Organisations.
The portal tracks dataset cataloguing, metadata preparation, standards and classifications, machine-readable identifiers and statistical quality checks.
The initiative aims to strengthen the National Data System and support interoperable, evidence-based policymaking while maintaining responsible data-sharing practices.

national.headline: ICAR researchers develop AI-based system to track Mithun behaviour
facts: Researchers at ICAR–National Research Centre on Mithun, Nagaland, developed an AI-based system for real-time detection and tracking of Mithun behaviour in a farm environment.
The reported approach is non-contact and uses cameras to monitor animal behaviour.
The research identifies possible applications in animal health, welfare, breeding and reproductive management.
Mithun (Bos frontalis), also called the “Cattle of the Hills,” has livelihood, food-security and cultural importance for tribal communities in Northeast India.
national.summary: The Agriculture Ministry reported the ICAR research on 8 September, describing a camera-based AI approach to Mithun monitoring. international.headline: WHO summary highlights association between tobacco use and infertility
facts: WHO issued its tobacco-and-infertility knowledge summary on 8 September 2026.
The summary reports that a review of studies from 2000–2026 found women who currently smoke had a 40% higher infertility risk than non-smokers.
WHO states that infertility affects one in six people of reproductive age at some point in their lifetime.
The summary also discusses associations with male reproductive dysfunction, second-hand smoke exposure and lower success rates in some fertility treatments.
WHO recommends that health-care providers explain reproductive risks and offer evidence-based tobacco-cessation support.
international.summary: WHO’s new knowledge summary draws attention to evidence linking tobacco use with reproductive health risks in women and men, including possible effects from second-hand smoke. WHO recommends cessation advice in health-care settings; evidence for newer nicotine products remains less established.
international.staticLink: Public health determinants, reproductive health and tobacco-control measures.
international.prelimsTakeaway: WHO’s 8 September 2026 publication is a tobacco knowledge summary on infertility; it reports an association, not a claim that smoking is the sole cause of infertility.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how integrating tobacco cessation into reproductive and primary health services can advance preventive healthcare.

# 2. Key findings

|---|---|
| Women who currently smoke | **40% higher infertility risk** than non-smokers |
| Infertility prevalence | **One in six** people of reproductive age affected at some point in their lifetime |

# 3. Recommendation and exam focus
- **WHO recommendation:** Health-care providers to explain reproductive risks and offer evidence-based tobacco-cessation support

- ⚠ **Trap:** The **40%** figure is a higher risk reported for women who currently smoke compared with non-smokers; it is not a claim that smoking is the sole cause of infertility.
> Exam angle: Recall the **WHO** summary’s date, evidence and distinction between association and sole causation.

international.headline: UNCTAD warns Hormuz disruption risks could weigh disproportionately on smaller firms
facts: UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) released its analysis on Strait of Hormuz disruption risks on 8 September 2026.
UNCTAD says small and medium-sized enterprises account for about 90% of businesses, 70% of global employment and 50% of global GDP.
The analysis highlights energy, transport, insurance and financing costs as channels that can pressure smaller firms.
It warns that firms in developing economies may remain excluded from value chains even after headline trade recovers.
international.summary: UNCTAD’s analysis examines how disruption around a strategic trade chokepoint can transmit costs to firms well beyond the immediate region. It emphasizes the exposure of SMEs and the importance of trade finance, liquidity and logistics access, especially in developing economies.
international.staticLink: Globalisation, trade chokepoints, supply-chain resilience and the role of SMEs in development.
international.prelimsTakeaway: UNCTAD identifies SMEs as representing about 90% of businesses, 70% of global employment and half of global GDP.
international.mainsAngle: Analyse how geopolitical disruption to maritime trade routes can affect inclusive growth through energy, freight and credit-cost channels.

international.headline: UNESCO announces six laureates of its 2026 International Literacy Prizes
facts: UNESCO announced six International Literacy Prize laureates on 8 September 2026 during the global literacy celebration in Chiapas, Mexico.
The UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize laureates were programmes from Colombia, the Kingdom of the Netherlands and Nigeria.
The UNESCO Confucius Prize for Literacy laureates were programmes from Lebanon, Mexico and Thailand.
Each laureate receives an endowment of US$30,000, a medal and a diploma.
The 2026 theme was “Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity.”
international.summary: The awards recognized six programmes advancing literacy in varied contexts, including multilingual education, displaced learners, out-of-school children and community learning. The announcement formed part of UNESCO’s International Literacy Day global celebration in Mexico.
international.staticLink: Literacy as a human right, inclusive education and lifelong learning under SDG 4.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 2026 UNESCO International Literacy Prizes comprise the King Sejong and Confucius prizes, with three laureates in each category.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how multilingual and community-based literacy initiatives can reduce educational exclusion and support social inclusion.
